html:
Nelson Mandela was a South African leader in the struggle against apartheid who spent 27 years in prison and then served as the country's first black president, from 1994 to 1999, after its first fully democratic election.

He was born in Mvezo into the Thembu royal family, a Xhosa people, and studied law at Fort Hare and in Johannesburg, where he opened a law firm with Oliver Tambo. He joined the African National Congress (ANC) in 1943 and helped found its Youth League.

  • 1950s: he led protests against apartheid laws and supported the Freedom Charter of 1955. He was tried for treason and acquitted.
  • 1960 to 1961: after the Sharpeville massacre the ANC was banned, and he helped found its armed wing, Umkhonto we Sizwe.
  • 1964: at the Rivonia Trial he was sentenced to life in prison. He spent most of the next 18 years on Robben Island.

Over the years he became the world's best-known political prisoner, while young people rose against the state in the Soweto uprising and foreign sanctions grew. President F. W. de Klerk freed him in February 1990. The two negotiated the end of white minority rule and shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993. As president, Mandela stressed reconciliation, set up the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, and stepped down after one term.
sum: Nelson Mandela was a South African leader in the struggle against apartheid who spent 27 years in prison and then served as the country's first black president, from 1994 to 1999, after its first fully democratic election.
